boundaries: The goal is a general CLI that helps agents understand, change and prove things about code with less total effort and context. Passing the recorded examples does not establish that product goal.

The analyzer and SDK must not branch on benchmark repository names, paths, revisions or expected patches. Explicit user rules may select sources and uses; they cannot bypass language semantics or unsupported effects.
Demonstrated items retain their finite scope. Broader requirements need unfamiliar projects, independent language examples and complete agent-cost accounting.

The existing agent comparison used an older Luna model on two Rust tasks. The fr runs consumed more calls, context and time. There is no established general token or cost advantage, and no matched Sonnet or delegated-agent result here.
Current evidence means the recorded input hashes still match. It does not establish that every dependency was recorded; the independent behavior checks must also run.

Parsing a language does not imply full analysis or editing support. Dynamic imports, package initialization effects, runtime dispatch, merging namespace packages from multiple roots and wildcard export insertion remain limits of the current Python analysis or writer.
A proof about a model, a correct source location and a passing runtime test establish different things. Proofs about the source implementation require an explicit checked connection.

Saved findings about source code cannot track reStructuredText (RST) files directly. Boltons' documentation uses an exact text replacement with a saved review, undo and an explicit check of every named Python object. The earlier more-itertools task used an unchanged Python module as its independent observation.

evidence.scope: Matched previous and current SDK storage sessions on three familiar projects, with fresh baselines and full answer agreement. The direct CLI/Python comparison has its own current record.
Nine scalar cases; exact AST links, omissions and stale refusal.
Finite package fixtures, clean agreement, repair and feature replay.
Two pinned full Python repositories; deterministic bug/feature delivery with interruption.
288 samples on six finite scalar workloads; whole-analysis reuse only.
224 model cases and native process interruption boundaries; not power loss.
Current Rust rename and parameter removal on a fixed fixture, with 49 compiled public results and exact patch reversal.
Three Boolean model relations; no source implementation connection between the descriptions.
Four comparison trials, three diagnostics; three successes, ordinary feature failed. Rust only.
Eleven declared Rust/Python features; eighteen cases, compiler and runtime checks, explicit refusals.

14 declared Python rules; 476 authored programs and 952 original/renamed cases, including 18 CLI refusals. Checks this declared set of Python examples; broader real-project requirements need separate results.

Current indexing on fixed sources; unchanged smaller workloads match original answers. Rust language fixes intentionally change repository answers. The original complete-output speed comparison is audited against its original source.

Historical frozen utility baseline; thirty identity-adapter cells on the preceding analyzer. Runtime replay uses retained original sources. This report cannot qualify the revised analyzer or close B.repository-flow.
Current maintenance replay of four familiar packages with one executable. The first unread Stringcase result remains checked separately at its original checker and procedure.
Three original projects, seven change controls each, and checked Rust and Python rename delivery.

Three repetitions on glob, Boltons and first reserved JMESPath. Saved and fresh answers agree across first use, unchanged reuse and a single-file edit. Includes startup, validation, discovery, storage and complete program requests; no agent savings claim.

Complete CLI, fresh Python, running Python and saved-answer sessions on three familiar projects. All 135 answers agree; includes startup, edits, validation, shutdown and cleanup. No live-agent savings claim.

Both Rust/Python directions, each repeated after renaming and moving; 9,030 exhaustive input pairs and eleven signed-64-bit boundary pairs per translation. A finite behavior check, not a general proof.

Nine Python effect examples repeated after renaming and moving, with two runtime inputs each. Exact source locations and visible model/runtime disagreement; handlers and shared objects remain unsupported.

Plain string conversions and twelve read-only string methods, repeated after renaming and moving. Independent Python outcomes, conservative receiver checks and saved-answer controls. No runtime exception-safety claim.
Current replay of all 21 change controls and both renames. All projects are familiar; the original first Humanize result remains separate.
